claims.claim_text: The piece is a simulation study of canon formation
claims.evidence_quote: I built a simulation to find out ... This post is the less formal version
claims.reasoning: Title accurately names the topic and method; source confirms a simulation plus informal writeup.

claims.claim_text: Simulated cultural markets show patronage and feedback manufacture canons: quality filters but capital decides
claims.evidence_quote: Story 3 wins. Quality acts as a loose filter ... the vast middle ground ... is dominated by capital and luck
claims.reasoning: Summary compresses the verdict plus the patronage-reshuffle results with identical meaning.

claims.claim_text: We remember under 20 of thousands; patrons, not merit, may have chosen
claims.evidence_quote: We remember fewer than 20 ... were they the ones who happened to have the right patron, the right court position
claims.reasoning: Count exact; the causal reading stays hedged with may have, matching the source question form.

claims.claim_text: Vienna had 200 to 500 active composers; IMSLP catalogs over 3,400 survivors
claims.evidence_quote: somewhere between 200 and 500 active composers at any given time ... IMSLP catalogs over 3,400 composers whose work survived in some form
claims.reasoning: Both figures exact against source; survivors correctly renders whose work survived in some form.

claims.claim_text: History cannot rerun; Haydn without Esterhazy patronage is empirically unanswerable
claims.evidence_quote: We can't rewind history and run it again ... If the Esterhazy family had hired a different Kapellmeister instead of Haydn, would we still know Haydn's name? We literally cannot answer that question empirically
claims.reasoning: Direct rephrase of the rewind-history passage and the Haydn question with the empirical-unanswerable verdict kept.

claims.claim_text: Project tests three competing stories of canon formation
claims.evidence_quote: I set up the project to test three competing hypotheses. Each tells a different story
claims.reasoning: Exact restatement of the three-hypotheses setup.

claims.claim_text: Story 1 Cream Rises: quality wins over time; replayed history yields same canon
claims.evidence_quote: genuine quality wins. If you replayed history with different patrons, you'd end up with roughly the same canon
claims.reasoning: Matches Story 1 including the replay-history consequence.

claims.claim_text: Story 2 Money Writes History: early exposure becomes familiarity, then canon; quality nearly irrelevant
claims.evidence_quote: A composer with a wealthy patron gets performed; audiences grow to like what they hear ... that familiarity gets retroactively interpreted as quality ... Quality is almost irrelevant
claims.reasoning: Chain and closer match Story 2 wording with identical meaning.

claims.claim_text: Story 3 Floors and Ceilings: extremes decided by quality, middle by luck and money
claims.evidence_quote: The truly terrible never succeed no matter how much money ... The truly transcendent sometimes break through ... for the vast majority in the middle ... depends on luck, money, and timing
claims.reasoning: Faithful compression of the floors-and-ceilings story.

claims.claim_text: Job-market analogy: top and bottom rank easily; middle hires depend on luck
claims.evidence_quote: The very best candidate and the very worst are easy to rank. But among the twenty pretty good candidates, who gets hired often comes down to who knew someone
claims.reasoning: Analogy restated with identical meaning; luck covers knew-someone, good-day, pile-top instances fairly.

claims.claim_text: Model combines three documented mechanisms to quantify their joint canon effect
claims.evidence_quote: three phenomena that are individually well-documented ... but whose combined effect on cultural canons hasn't been quantified
claims.reasoning: Matches the mechanisms section framing exactly.

claims.claim_text: Mere exposure: liking grows with familiarity; Zajonc 1968, Bornstein 1989 r equals 0.26
claims.evidence_quote: Zajonc demonstrated this in 1968, and Bornstein's 1989 meta-analysis across 208 experiments confirmed it with an average effect size of r = 0.26
claims.reasoning: Names, years, and effect size exact; [reported] correctly marks external-study attribution. The 208-experiment detail is thinned but not contradicted.

claims.claim_text: Exposure advantage contaminates sincere judgment; money set the exposure
claims.evidence_quote: the judging is contaminated by the exposure, and the exposure was determined by money
claims.reasoning: Near-verbatim restatement of the contamination passage.

claims.claim_text: Social influence snowballs popularity; Salganik MusicLab 2006 ranked same song 1st or 40th
claims.evidence_quote: The Salganik MusicLab experiment (2006) ... the same song could rank 1st in one version of the world and 40th in another
claims.reasoning: Year and both ranks exact; [reported] marks the external study. Participant and song counts thinned without contradiction.

claims.claim_text: Cumulative advantage magnifies small starts; Merton Matthew Effect compounds court posts
claims.evidence_quote: The sociologist Robert Merton called this the Matthew Effect ... A composer who secures a court position at age 20 accumulates decades of performances
claims.reasoning: Matches the rich-get-richer mechanism, the Merton attribution, and the court-post example.

claims.claim_text: Open question: what happens when all three interact over generations
claims.evidence_quote: What I wanted to know is: when you put all three together in a system and let them interact over many generations, what happens?
claims.reasoning: Direct rephrase of the stated research question.

claims.claim_text: Simulation uses producers, consumers, gatekeepers with independent quality and capital scores
claims.evidence_quote: three types of agents: producers (composers/artists), consumers (audiences), and gatekeepers (critics, curators, playlist editors) ... a quality score drawn randomly ... and a capital score drawn independently
claims.reasoning: Agent types and independent score draws all stated; independent correctly renders drawn independently.

claims.claim_text: Quality and capital are uncorrelated; wealth does not make talent
claims.evidence_quote: Quality and capital are uncorrelated. Being wealthy doesn't make you talented.
claims.reasoning: Verbatim restatement.

claims.claim_text: Capital buys exposure; consumers add quality, exposure, social signals; success feeds exposure
claims.evidence_quote: Producers with more capital get more exposure. Consumers form opinions based on actual quality plus the mere exposure effect plus social signals. Success feeds back into more exposure
claims.reasoning: All three dynamics restated with identical meaning.

claims.claim_text: Thousands of runs; 1,000 producers, 10,000 consumers; 360 plus per condition with power analysis
claims.evidence_quote: I ran this thousands of times ... 1,000 producers and 10,000 consumers ... ran 360+ per condition for the main experiments, with formal power analysis
claims.reasoning: All four scale figures exact against source.

claims.claim_text: Results favor capital-plus-feedback over pure quality across experiments
claims.evidence_quote: Story 3 wins ... the biggest distortion isn't that audiences follow trends. It's that some artists never get heard in the first place
claims.reasoning: Theme verdict consistent with the ablation and replay results; fair synthesis.

claims.claim_text: Visible social influence significantly weakens quality-success link, p below 0.0001
claims.evidence_quote: the correlation between actual quality and commercial success drops significantly (p < 0.0001 across 360 runs per condition)
claims.reasoning: Significance level and direction exact; p below 0.0001 renders p < 0.0001 identically.

claims.claim_text: Charts push us from independent judgment toward optimizing a popularity proxy
claims.evidence_quote: systematically pushes us away from independent judgment ... We use popularity as a proxy for quality, then optimize for the proxy
claims.reasoning: Identical-meaning compression of the recommendation-algorithm passage.

claims.claim_text: Talent held fixed across 200 runs; only patronage reshuffled
claims.evidence_quote: I held talent constant. Every simulated composer kept the exact same quality score. I only reshuffled their resources ... Then I ran it 200 times
claims.reasoning: Design and run count exact; patronage fairly names who-had-wealthy-patrons resources.

claims.claim_text: Counterfactual distance 0.88; top-decile talent has 1-in-4 fame chance; middle is lottery
claims.evidence_quote: The counterfactual distance was 0.88 ... Only the top 10% of talent had a meaningful shot at fame ... and even then it was only about 1 in 4 ... canonical status was effectively a lottery
claims.reasoning: Distance, decile, 1-in-4, and lottery wording all exact.

claims.claim_text: Without Esterhazy hire, Haydn likely joins forgotten hundreds despite excellence
claims.evidence_quote: If the Esterhazys had hired someone else, Haydn would very likely be one of the hundreds of forgotten 18th-century composers ... Not because he wasn't excellent
claims.reasoning: Hedge likely preserves very likely; excellence qualifier kept.

claims.claim_text: Ablation: full 0.32, no-social 0.35, equal-capital 0.46, quality-only 0.46
claims.evidence_quote: Full model (everything active): quality-canon correlation = 0.32 ... No social influence ... 0.35 ... Equal capital ... 0.46 ... Quality only ... 0.46
claims.reasoning: All four correlations exact with correct condition labels.

claims.claim_text: Equalizing resources raises quality link 44 percent; exclusion distorts most
claims.evidence_quote: equalizing starting resources jumps the quality-canon correlation by 44%. The biggest distortion isn't that audiences follow trends. It's that some artists never get heard in the first place
claims.reasoning: Percentage and biggest-distortion reading exact.

claims.claim_text: Modern gate: major labels reach playlists first; downstream is noise amplification
claims.evidence_quote: only major-label artists get on those playlists to begin with. Capital gates access to the exposure pipeline, and everything downstream of that is noise amplification
claims.reasoning: Near-verbatim restatement of the modern-mapping passage.

claims.claim_text: Stylized Vienna: 300 composers, distance 0.97, only 2.5 percent shared
claims.evidence_quote: 300 composers ... The counterfactual distance was 0.97 ... Only 2.5% of canonical composers were shared between any two alternate histories
claims.reasoning: All three figures exact.

claims.claim_text: Winners likely excellent, but dozens of equals lost the patronage lottery
claims.evidence_quote: The winners in our timeline were very likely excellent ... But dozens of equally excellent composers were lost to history because they drew the short straw in the patronage lottery
claims.reasoning: Hedge and dozens figure kept; lottery renders short-straw identically.

claims.claim_text: Manufacturing taste means losers were not meaningfully worse
claims.evidence_quote: That's what manufacturing taste means. Not that the winners were bad. That the losers weren't meaningfully worse.
claims.reasoning: Verbatim definition restated.

claims.claim_text: Robustness plus-minus 50 percent: steep capital-to-exposure conversion erases quality fastest
claims.evidence_quote: I varied every parameter by ±50%. The single most important factor is how steeply money converts into attention ... quality barely matters
claims.reasoning: Range and most-important-factor claims exact.

claims.claim_text: Steep playlist reach gaps predict fame decoupled from quality
claims.evidence_quote: When a major label can buy a front-page Spotify placement reaching 50 million listeners while an independent artist's self-promotion reaches 500 ... quality has very little to do with who becomes famous
claims.reasoning: Fair reading of the 50M-vs-500 illustration and its prediction.

claims.claim_text: Story 3 wins: quality sets floor and ceiling; capital and luck rule middle
claims.evidence_quote: Story 3 wins. Quality acts as a loose filter. It sets a floor below which you can't succeed and a ceiling above which you probably will. But the vast middle ground ... is dominated by capital and luck
claims.reasoning: Near-verbatim verdict restatement.

claims.claim_text: Implications worth spelling out below
claims.evidence_quote: There are a few implications worth spelling out.
claims.reasoning: Transition line matches the source segue; propositional content minimal but accurate.

claims.claim_text: Bach greatest only among heard, published, preserved; equals may never have survived
claims.evidence_quote: Bach is the greatest composer who ever lived among those who had the resources to be heard, published, and preserved. There may have been equally gifted composers whose music was never performed, never published, and never survived
claims.reasoning: Triple qualifier kept verbatim in effect; hedge may preserved.

claims.claim_text: Feedback loops run faster today; playlists decide in hours, patronage took decades
claims.evidence_quote: operate faster in the age of algorithmic recommendations. An 18th-century patronage decision played out over decades. A Spotify playlist placement plays out in hours
claims.reasoning: Speed comparison and both timescales exact.

claims.claim_text: Leverage is wider exposure; blind auditions lifted women hires 5 to 25 percent
claims.evidence_quote: The highest-leverage intervention isn't better judgment, it's wider exposure. Blind auditions ... the proportion of women hired by major US orchestras went from 5% to 25%
claims.reasoning: Leverage claim and both percentages exact; [reported] correctly marks the external historical fact.

claims.claim_text: Canon-as-best confuses metric with thing; curricula built on forgotten proxy
claims.evidence_quote: We use survived into the canon as a proxy for was the best, then build entire curricula and cultural narratives on that proxy, forgetting it was ever a proxy at all
claims.reasoning: Identical-meaning compression of the metric-proxy passage.

claims.claim_text: Caveats bound what the model can and cannot tell us
claims.evidence_quote: I want to be honest about what this can and can't tell us.
claims.reasoning: Section frame restated; introduces the three concessions accurately.

claims.claim_text: Quality may be partly constituted socially, making decomposition ill-posed
claims.evidence_quote: If quality is partly constituted by social processes ... then the whole decomposition may be ill-posed
claims.reasoning: Hedge may kept on both halves; philosophical caveat preserved.

claims.claim_text: Calibration leaps from teens judging pop over weeks to aristocrats over decades
claims.evidence_quote: studied American teenagers evaluating pop songs over weeks. Generalizing to 18th-century European aristocrats evaluating orchestral music over decades requires a leap of faith
claims.reasoning: Both populations and timescales kept; leap of faith rendered as leaps without drift.

claims.claim_text: Model omits genre, discourse, technology, politics; direction robust, magnitudes uncertain
claims.evidence_quote: doesn't include: genre formation, critical discourse, technological change, cultural politics ... The direction of the effects is robust ... the precise magnitudes are uncertain
claims.reasoning: Omission list and robust-direction versus uncertain-magnitude split both exact.

claims.claim_text: Bach was not Bieber, but closer than expected
claims.evidence_quote: Not exactly, but closer than I expected.
claims.reasoning: Closing answer compressed with meaning intact.

claims.claim_text: Bieber analogy gets mechanism right but quality floor wrong; court posts demanded skill
claims.evidence_quote: The Bieber analogy gets the mechanism right but the quality floor wrong ... to hold a court position you had to write music that worked for liturgical services, entertain aristocrats, train choirs, improvise fugues
claims.reasoning: Mechanism-right floor-wrong split plus the skill-demand evidence all stated.

claims.claim_text: Bach was excellent and well-positioned; positioning matters more than merit gap
claims.evidence_quote: He was excellent AND well-positioned. But the simulation tells us the AND is doing most of the work, and the second half matters more than the first
claims.reasoning: Excellent-plus-positioned and second-half-matters-more both kept.

claims.claim_text: Famous surgeon among fifty equals: profile led to talks, book, best reputation
claims.evidence_quote: one surgeon who gets famous out of fifty equally skilled surgeons ... profile in the New York Times, which led to speaking invitations, which led to a book deal, which led to a reputation as the best surgeon in the country
claims.reasoning: Analogy chain restated with count and steps intact.

claims.claim_text: Leipzig job decided it; 20 to 50 equals forgotten for missing that post
claims.evidence_quote: there were probably 20 to 50 of his contemporaries who were equally great, whose names we will never know, because they didn't get that job
claims.reasoning: Range and cause exact; decided-it fairly renders the job counterfactual.

claims.claim_text: Canon is one of hundreds of valid possible canons, treated as inevitable
claims.evidence_quote: it's one canon out of hundreds of equally valid ones we could have ended up with, and we treat it as if it were inevitable
claims.reasoning: Hundreds qualifier and inevitability framing both kept.

claims.claim_text: Taste itself was manufactured: survivors set harmonic foundations we judge by
claims.evidence_quote: It's not just that the canon was manufactured. It's that our taste was manufactured along with it ... His harmonic language, his structures, his aesthetic sensibility: these are the foundations of how we hear and judge music today
claims.reasoning: Title-meaning claim restated with the harmonic-foundations mechanism intact.

claims.claim_text: Future canons will reward distribution and algorithms over musical merit
claims.evidence_quote: if the mechanisms in this simulation are right, then whoever survives into the canon of the 2000s will have more to do with who had the best distribution deals and the most favorable algorithms than with who made the best music
claims.reasoning: Content matches but the source's conditional if the mechanisms are right and the honestly-don't-know hedge are dropped, stating a contingent prediction as absolute fact. At most Partially supported per the hedge rule; low-stakes closing speculation, so Minor.

fail_list: C52 states the future-canon prediction absolutely, dropping the source conditional 'if the mechanisms in this simulation are right'
